captions: Capture: the 16 cycles before the trigger come from the analyser's buffer, recorded before the trigger fired.
Cycle 0, the trigger sample: win_wr == 1 AND addr == 0x80 (win_wr = 1, addr = 0x80).
Cycle 1: count changes from 0x0003 to 0x1234, one clock after the write strobe: the register loads on the clock edge that ends it.

stages.name: Request
captions: Request, in plain English: "First write 3 to COUNT. Then capture count, win_wr and the shell's ADDR byte when the shell writes the COUNT register (win_wr is 1 and addr is 0x80), 16 cycles before and 32 after. The write that triggers it puts 0x1234 in COUNT. Afterwards read COUNT back."

stages.name: Plan
captions: Plan: win_wr is u_shell.u_core.win_wr; addr is u_shell.u_core.frame[1]; count is u_dut.count. Trigger: win_wr == 1 AND addr == 0x80. A 1024-sample window, the smallest that holds the 16 cycles before and 32 after that were asked for.

stages.name: Build
captions: Build: the logic analyser added to the design, Vivado 2026.1, 418.1 s, every check passed (worst setup slack 3.06 ns). Programmed into the board's memory; build ID d2b75378 read back over JTAG before arming.

stages.name: Arm and capture
captions: Armed. Over the serial link: before arming COUNT = 0x3; after arming COUNT = 0x1234, the write that fires the trigger.

stages.name: Answer
captions: Answer: count was 0x0003 from cycle -16 to 0, then 0x1234 from cycle 1 to 32.
Read back over the serial link: COUNT = 0x00001234, the value the capture shows. Programming and capture took 64.7 s, inside the recommended operating conditions.

alt: Waveform of win_wr, addr and count from cycle -16 to 32 around the trigger: win_wr is 1 only at cycle 0, addr holds 0x80, count is 0x0003 up to cycle 0 and 0x1234 from cycle 1.
